name: Shallot
grown_as: The shallot. William grows 'Simiane' (AG 131), a long banana shallot grown from seed, which usually makes one long torpedo-shaped bulb per plant with coppery pink-red skin rather than a cluster. Shallots grown from sets divide into clusters of 4 to 12 bulbs. ⚠️ CHECK: one bulb per plant. Not drawn in flower: shallots seldom flower.
habit: Grown from seed: a few upright hollow leaves 25 to 40 cm from one long bulb that swells at the soil surface.

leaf.arrangement: In two ranks from the neck of each bulb, many bulbs together making a clump
leaf.outline: Long, narrow, hollow, round to half-round tube, 20 to 40 cm by 0.5 to 1 cm, thinner than onion
leaf.base: A sheath wrapping the neck of its bulb

fruit: Not drawn: shallots rarely flower; when they do it is a small round greenish-white head like an onion's.
seedling: A single thin grass-like seed leaf bent like a hairpin with the black seed case on its tip, as in onion, then thin hollow leaves.
winter: Bulbs are lifted and dried in summer and stored. Sets planted in winter or early spring show a few thin leaves.

leaf: a long thin hollow round tube, not flat
set: seedlings: one thin seed leaf bent like a hairpin, the seed case on its tip
young: a few thin hollow leaves from one long bulb starting to swell
crop: one long torpedo-shaped bulb with coppery pink-red papery skin, half on top of the soil

look_alikes: Onion grows into one round bulb, not a cluster. Garlic makes a bulb of cloves under one shared skin, with flat leaves. Potato onions (multiplier onions) are the same group and look much the same.
